title: Choir Rehearsal Planning Guide
content:
# Choir Rehearsal Planning Guide

This guide helps ward and stake choir directors plan effective rehearsals that prepare the choir spiritually and musically.

---

## Sample 4-Week Choir Rehearsal Plan

This plan prepares a choir to perform one hymn arrangement or anthem.

### Week 1: Introduction & Note Learning

**Duration:** 45-60 minutes

**Opening (5 min)**
- Opening prayer
- Brief spiritual thought related to the music's message

**Warm-Up (10 min)**
- Physical stretches
- Humming exercises
- Vowel unification (Mee-May-Mah-Moh-Moo)
- Scale exercises in the key of the piece

**Note Learning (30 min)**
- Play through the piece once (director or recording)
- Teach each section their notes separately:
  - Sopranos/Altos together
  - Tenors/Basses together
- Focus on pitch accuracy, not dynamics yet
- Work on difficult passages slowly

**Closing (5 min)**
- Sing through once, mistakes and all
- Assign homework: practice part with recording
- Closing prayer

---

### Week 2: Rhythm & Ensemble

**Opening (5 min)**
- Prayer
- Share a verse related to the hymn text

**Warm-Up (10 min)**
- Same warm-ups, add rhythm exercises
- Count rhythms of difficult passages together

**Rehearsal (30 min)**
- Sing through the piece together
- Stop and fix rhythm problems
- Work on entrances and cutoffs
- Ensure all parts are learning their notes
- Practice transitions between sections

**Closing (5 min)**
- Full sing-through
- Note improvement areas
- Assign continued practice

---

### Week 3: Blend & Dynamics

**Opening (5 min)**
- Prayer
- Discuss the meaning of the text

**Warm-Up (10 min)**
- Focus on blending exercises
- Match vowels across sections
- Practice crescendo/decrescendo on a single chord

**Rehearsal (30 min)**
- Sing through with attention to dynamics (loud/soft)
- Work on blend—no individual voices should stand out
- Add expression markings
- Practice beginning and ending clearly
- Run difficult sections multiple times

**Closing (5 min)**
- Full performance run-through
- Positive feedback and areas to polish

---

### Week 4: Polish & Performance Prep

**Opening (5 min)**
- Prayer for the Spirit to attend the performance
- Read a quote about sacred music

**Warm-Up (10 min)**
- Light warm-up—don't tire voices before performance
- Focus on confidence and relaxation

**Rehearsal (30 min)**
- Multiple full run-throughs
- Work on stage presence and posture
- Practice entering and exiting the stand area
- Discuss logistics (when to stand, where to look)
- Final polish on trouble spots

**Closing (5 min)**
- Final encouragement
- Remind of performance time/date
- Closing prayer

---

## Rehearsal Best Practices

### Start on Time
- Respect everyone's schedule
- Begin with prayer even if not everyone is there

### Be Prepared
- Know the music better than the choir
- Have a written rehearsal plan
- Mark your score with teaching points

### Stay Positive
- Praise what's going well
- Correct gently: "Let's try that again with more breath support"
- Never embarrass individuals

### Balance Sections
- Don't neglect any voice part
- Give tenors and altos special attention (harmony is harder)
- Help basses understand their foundational role

### Keep It Moving
- Don't spend too long on one spot
- Come back to difficult passages later
- Variety maintains energy

---

## Troubleshooting Common Choir Problems

### Pitch Problems
| Issue | Solution |
|-------|----------|
| Choir sings flat | Work on breath support, think "up" |
| Choir sings sharp | Relax tension, don't push |
| One section off | Isolate and fix, then recombine |
| Unisons not together | Practice in octaves first |

### Rhythm Problems
| Issue | Solution |
|-------|----------|
| Not together | Clap/speak rhythms, use metronome |
| Rushing | Slow down, feel the steady pulse |
| Dragging | Lighter articulation, energy |
| Wrong note values | Write in counts, practice slowly |

### Blend Problems
| Issue | Solution |
|-------|----------|
| One voice too loud | Kindly ask them to listen more |
| Sections not blending | Unify vowels, adjust positioning |
| Vibrato issues | Ask for "straighter" tone in choir |
| Harsh sound | Work on relaxation, softer onsets |

---

## Choosing Music for Ward Choir

### Consider Your Resources
- How many singers do you have?
- Voice part distribution (often light on tenors)
- Skill level of accompanist
- Time available to prepare

### Appropriate Difficulty
- Start with hymn arrangements (familiar melodies)
- Progress to simple anthems
- Challenge gradually

### Match the Occasion
- Christmas: Christmas hymns and carols
- Easter: Resurrection-themed music
- Sacrament: Atonement, testimony themes
- Fast Sunday: Gratitude, service themes

### Resources for Music
- LDS.org Church Music Library
- Deseret Book choir arrangements
- Simple hymn descants and arrangements
- Public domain hymns from other Christian traditions (if appropriate)

---

## Sample Annual Choir Calendar

| Month | Occasion | Suggested Theme |
|-------|----------|----------------|
| January | New Year | Goals, Commitment |
| February | Valentine's | Love, Charity |
| March | Pre-Easter | Atonement |
| April | Easter Sunday | Resurrection |
| May | Mother's Day | Families, Love |
| June | Father's Day | Families, Service |
| July | Pioneer Day | Faith, Pioneers |
| August | Back to School | Learning, Growth |
| September | Fall | Gratitude, Harvest |
| October | General Conference | Prophets, Revelation |
| November | Thanksgiving | Gratitude |
| December | Christmas | Nativity, Joy |

---

## Working with Your Accompanist

1. **Communicate early** - Give music well in advance
2. **Discuss tempo** - Agree on how fast/slow
3. **Plan intros** - How many measures before choir enters?
4. **Rehearse together** - At least once before performance
5. **Express gratitude** - Accompanists serve faithfully

---

## Inviting the Spirit Through Music

### Before Rehearsal
- Pray for the Spirit to attend
- Study the text and its message
- Prepare your heart to teach

### During Rehearsal
- Keep the focus on worship, not performance
- Share brief spiritual insights
- Connect the music to gospel principles

### Before Performance
- Gather the choir for prayer
- Remind them of the purpose: helping others worship
- Express confidence and gratitude

Remember: Choir music in the Church is ministry, not performance. Every rehearsal is an opportunity to grow closer to the Savior through His music.
